title: Bram and the Parish
premise: Rosalind Whitlock, a concierge at the fading Hotel Meridian, is paid a retainer by an elderly client, Bram Ashford, who insists that his sister's death last year was not murder — but will be. When Bram vanishes and Rosalind finds his name in a parish ledger disguised as donation records, they uncover a decades-old inheritance scheme sustained by forged deaths and coerced silence. As Rosalind decodes the ledger with help from Bram's estranged granddaughter, they realize the next 'death' scheduled in its pages is their own. In the end, Rosalind exposes the scheme at the parish's centenary service, choosing truth over the loyalty that kept the town complicit — and inherits, unexpectedly, the trust of a community that once made them invisible.
about_author: Rosalind Nakamura spent twelve years working night desks in grand hotels across three continents, collecting the small tragedies guests leave behind in lobby conversations. She writes mysteries about people whose professions make them professionally unnoticeable.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A meticulous elderly guest, Bram Ashford, pays six months upfront for one service: to be told if anyone asks about him after he leaves. He claims his sister was murdered a year ago and that the same fate awaits someone else. Rosalind, unsettled by his certainty, accepts. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Checkout Without a Checkout
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Bram disappears overnight, leaving no bill, no forwarding address, and a keycard for room 411 that no longer exists on the hotel's system. The front desk records have been altered — by someone with access. Emotional beat: the first vertigo of realizing the hotel itself is lying.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, with a flashback to Bram's confession. Following Bram's notes hidden in the hotel chapel's hymnal rack, Rosalind finds St. Aldhelm's parish ledger: donation entries where amounts encode dates and initials. His sister's name appears beside a sum matching her funeral date. Emotional beat: grief reframed as evidence.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rosalind and Nell Ashford. Nell arrives searching for her missing grandfather, convinced he's senile. Rosalind must decide whether to reveal what she knows or protect Bram's secrecy. They form a wary alliance over the ledger's cipher. Emotional beat: two strangers negotiating trust neither can afford.

chapters.title: Deaths on Paper
chapters.summary: POV Nell. Decoding reveals eleven names across forty years — parishioners recorded as dead who demonstrably lived, their inheritances quietly rerouted through the church's restoration fund. Someone has been erasing people while they breathe. Emotional beat: horror at how bureaucratic evil looks in ink.

chapters.title: The Warden
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The parish warden, Mr. Calloway — charming, generous, ubiquitous — begins appearing wherever Rosalind goes, offering help that feels like surveillance. A break-in at the hotel targets Bram's room. Rosalind realizes the concierge's invisibility is now their only armor. Emotional beat: being seen as a threat for the first time.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: POV Nell. Nell discovers her own father's name in the ledger — alive, listed dead, his estate funneled away — and learns he knew, and stayed silent to protect the family name. Her loyalty to her bloodline fractures against the truth. Emotional beat: betrayal as inheritance.

chapters.title: Room 411
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Following the ledger's final cipher, Rosalind finds the sealed fourth-floor room behind renovation hoarding — Bram is there, held by choice, guarding the original deeds. He confesses he helped build the scheme decades ago and has been paying it back ever since. Emotional beat: guilt as a life sentence.

chapters.title: The Centenary Service
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind and Nell. Calloway moves to finalize the next entry — Rosalind's own name appears dated for Sunday. At the packed centenary service, they trigger the fire alarm, seize the lectern, and read the ledger aloud as Calloway's allies scatter. Bram identifies himself publicly. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into testimony.

chapters.title: Long Stay
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Calloway is arrested; the estates begin returning; Bram, dying, asks Rosalind to witness his will leaving everything to the defrauded families. Nell takes a job at the Meridian's front desk. Rosalind finally registers under their own name instead of staying invisible. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
